speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your new movement disorder, could you describe the specific movements you are experiencing, such as tremors, stiffness, or involuntary jerking? Additionally, have you recently started, stopped, or changed the dosage of any psychiatric medications?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience an uncomfortable sensation of restlessness or an inner urge to keep moving, often relieved by pacing or shifting positions? Have you noticed any stiffness, tremors, or difficulty initiating voluntary movements like walking or speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: These symptoms are classic for akathisia, a common side effect of risperidone. I will adjust your medication regimen to alleviate this distressing restlessness while maintaining your psychiatric stability.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: To ensure we manage this safely, have you experienced any other side effects like muscle stiffness, tremors, or slowed movements? I will also need to check your vital signs to rule out other causes of agitation.
